title: Who may release, and checking before acquiring

questions.stem: Per this page, thread A calls `acquire()` on a `new Semaphore(1)`, and then thread B, which never acquired it, calls `release()`. What happens?

options.text: B's call throws IllegalMonitorStateException, since only A holds the permit
options.says: The page gives this exception to ReentrantLock, whose unlock is tied to the owning thread; a semaphore tracks no owner.

options.text: B's call blocks until A gives the permit back, since only one may exist
options.says: The page says release() never waits and a semaphore enforces no upper bound on its count.

options.text: B's call succeeds and adds a permit, since the count has no owner
options.says: The page says any thread can release a permit; this is what makes semaphores useful for signalling between threads.

questions.stem: Per this page, what is wrong with `if (sem.availablePermits() > 0) { sem.acquire(); }`, and what should be written instead?

options.text: The count can change between the two calls; call tryAcquire() instead
options.says: The page calls this a check-then-act race: another thread may take the permit after the check, while tryAcquire() checks and takes in one atomic step.

options.text: The count read takes a permit of its own; call release() after it
options.says: The page describes availablePermits() as a plain read of the current count; it takes nothing, so a release would inflate the count.

options.text: The count read is only a hint; call acquire() again in a loop
options.says: The page's fix is a single atomic tryAcquire(); repeating acquire() would take several permits, since a semaphore is not reentrant.
